newsitem.title: USA: "Romeo and Juliet" romances U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Romeo and Juliet" romances U.S. box office.

text.p: An MTV-style update of a Shakespeare play, complete with car chases and gunfights, opened at the top of the weekend box office, according to studio estimates released Sunday.

"William Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet", starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Claire Danes as the ill-fated lovers, pulled in $11.6 million despite playing on fewer screens than any other movie in the top 10. The movie averaged a strong $9,084 per screen.
"Sleepers" slipped to second with $8.2 million after two weeks at No. 1, while "High School High" fell to third in its second week. It grossed $5.1 million.

The two other new entries in the top 10 fared poorly. Bill Murray's elephant caper "Larger Than Life" opened in fourth with $4.2 million, despite playing on almost twice as many screens as "Romeo and Juliet" (2,433 vs. 1,277). Its per screen average was $1,726. "Larger Than Life" is released by MGM, which is owned by financier Kirk Kerkorian and Australia's Seven Network Ltd.

"Dear God", the headlining debut of former talk show host Greg Kinnear, was in a battle for eighth with Whoopi Goldberg's "The Associate." Both films reported estimated grosses of $3.2 million. "Dear God", with an average of $1,824, is released by Viacom Inc.'s Paramount Pictures.

Shakespeare is suddenly hot at the box office, with Al Pacino's "Richard III" documentary "Looking For Richard" and "Twelfth Night" recently opening. Kenneth Branagh's "Hamlet" opens Christmas Day, clocking in at 3 hours, 50 minutes plus intermission.

"William Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet" is released by News Corp's 20th Century Fox, and was directed by Australian Baz Luhrmann ("Strictly Ballroom"). Critics were favourable to the high-octane update. A Variety poll of critics in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington D.C. showed that 22 liked the movie, 14 did not and 14 were mixed.
The most successful Shakespeare movie at the box office was Franco Zeffirelli's "Romeo and Juliet", which made $42 million in 1968. That version starred Leonard Whiting and Olivia Hussey.
After three weeks, "Sleepers" has earned a total of $37.8 million. The youthful hi-jinks drama, released by Time Warner Inc.'s Warner Bros., stars Brad Pitt, Jason Patric and Robert De Niro.
"High School High", a classroom comedy starring Jon Lovitz, has a two-week total of $12.7 million. The movie is released by Sony Corp.'s TriStar Pictures.

At the other end of the scale, the addition of 100 screens was unable to prevent Warner Bros.' Oscar hopeful "Michael Collins" from falling out of the top 10. The controversial movie about the Irish Republican earned $2.3 million at the weekend from 848 screens. After four weeks, its total is $6.1 million and it stood at 11, down from eight last weekend.
